overall.statement: The deterministic local control plane, zero-side-effect execution path, bounded continuation controls, in-process MCP compatibility path, and proof publication reconciliation gate are directly reproducibly proven. USB/DFW Metro is a documented integration case, not a claim that this package is deployed as DFW Metro runtime infrastructure.

direct_proof.proves: The checked-in control-plane, contract, execution, recovery, continuation, checkpoint, governance, and adapter behaviors pass their automated tests.
direct_proof.does_not_prove: Independent external-provider trust, hosted distributed operation, or commercial production readiness.

direct_proof.proves: The extracted package passes its secret, path, dependency, and publication-surface audit.
direct_proof.does_not_prove: That an external deployment has been secured or that a provider has authenticated the package.

direct_proof.proves: A closed example plan compiles to a deterministic, digest-bound workflow.
direct_proof.does_not_prove: Model quality or live provider behavior.

direct_proof.proves: Two intentionally different in-process MCP client shapes can complete one compiled workflow through the bounded adapter boundary.
direct_proof.does_not_prove: Trustworthiness or compatibility of a particular external MCP provider.

direct_proof.proves: A proof receipt cannot publish a CURRENT claim unless a fresh exact read-only observation matches its target, deployment, rollback, timestamp, and fields.
direct_proof.does_not_prove: That a host adapter's supplied observation is truthful, or that a provider accepted a deployment.

proof_release_gate.current_claim_rule: CURRENT requires an exact matching fresh observation; otherwise publication is BLOCKED.
proof_release_gate.historical_rule: HISTORICAL and SUPERSEDED evidence remains traceable but does not satisfy a CURRENT claim.
proof_release_gate.provider_boundary: Host adapters supply read-only observations; the gate makes no network calls and stores no credentials.

consumer.name: USB Website Platform
consumer.role: USB used the harness for bounded continuation, checkpointing, focused verification selection, approval boundaries, handoffs, and rollback-aware evidence while building deterministic Site artifacts.

dfwmetro.statement: The harness was used during USB development and verification work for DFW Metro and the disposable DFWMow review lab. The generated customer-Site artifacts remained deterministic and model-free.
dfwmetro.production_evidence_scope: External DFW Metro state reported by the integration workflow and partially verified by browser readback; it is not proof that this package is deployed inside DFW Metro or that every production mutation was harness-executed.
dfwmetro.lab_evidence_scope: Latest disposable control-plane lab deployment: the three approved functions remained, public root, /usb-lab/, and preserved offline download returned 200, and an unauthenticated private-route probe returned 404. The earlier visibility-only deployment remains historical evidence.

result.finding: The prior DFWMow lab deployment reference was stale; live had advanced to 6ab3d15578d1a74798a1ffaa.

confirmed: The agent manifest declares submit_listing on POST /mcp.
live_reconciliation.scope: Demonstrates digest-bound, contract-validated, budgeted, hash-chained live reconciliation and drift reporting; the raw run remains owner-controlled and this does not prove hosted operation, authenticated providers, commercial readiness, or harness execution of every DFW mutation.

limitations: The package is a source-available extraction prototype, not a hosted service or published npm package.
Distributed leasing, hosted scheduling, external provider authentication, and real-provider compatibility remain separate work.
DFW Metro production state and DFWMow lab deployments are external evidence and remain governed by their own deployment, database, provider, and rollback rules.
The proof receipt records reproducible scope and boundaries; it does not grant authority to deploy, mutate data, contact a provider, or publish a customer Site.
